121	    
122	    tasks_data = tools_jsonl_load(args.input_task)
123	    db_schemas_data = tools_jsonl_load(args.input_db)
124	    db_schemas_data = {normalize_scenario_name(item["scenario"]): item for item in db_schemas_data}
125	    
126	    logger.info(f"Preparing batch requests for {len(tasks_data)} scenarios...")
127	    
128	    def create_request(task_item, error_msg=None):
129	        scenario_name = task_item["scenario"]
130	        schema_item = db_schemas_data[normalize_scenario_name(scenario_name)]
131	        tasks_list = "\n".join([f"{i+1}. {task}" for i, task in enumerate(task_item["tasks"])])
132	        schema_str = format_db_schema(schema_item["db_schema"])
133	        
134	        user_content = SAMPLE_DATA_GENERATION_USER_PROMPT.format(
135	            scenario_name=scenario_name,
136	            tasks_list=tasks_list,
137	            database_schema=schema_str
138	        )
139	        
140	        if error_msg and error_msg != "":
141	            user_content += f"\n\nAttention: You MUST avoid generating SQL codes that caused the following errors in previous attempts. You MUST refer the below guidelines to help you avoid generating errors:\n{error_msg}"
142	        
143	        messages = [
144	            {
145	                "role": "system",
146	                "content": SAMPLE_DATA_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT
147	            },
148	            {
149	                "role": "user",
150	                "content": user_content
151	            }
152	        ]
153	        
154	        return {
155	            "messages": messages,
156	            "temperature": 1.0,
157	            "max_tokens": 128_000,
158	            "model": args.model,
159	        }
160	    
161	    current_items = tasks_data
162	    current_requests = [create_request(item) for item in current_items]
163	    
164	    results = []
165	    client = GPTClient()
166	    max_retries = args.max_retry
167	    error_threshold = args.error_threshold
168	    
169	    history_error_messages = {}
170	    history_data_messages = {}
171	    total_successful = 0
172	    total_failed = 0
173	
174	    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
175	        if not current_requests:
176	            break
177	        
178	        logger.info(f"Sending batch requests (Attempt {attempt+1}/{max_retries+1}) count={len(current_requests)}...")
179	        responses = client.batch_chat_completion(current_requests, progress_bar=True)
180	        
181	        next_items = []
182	        next_requests = []
183	
184	        for task_item, response in zip(current_items, responses):
185	            scenario_name = task_item["scenario"]
186	            error_msg = set()
187	            sample_data = {}
188	            total_tables = 0
189	            total_inserts = 0
190	            error_ratio = 1.0
191	            
192	            if not response:
193	                logger.error(f"Failed to generate sample data for {scenario_name}: Empty response")
194	            else:
195	                try:
196	                    logger.info(f"Processing response for {scenario_name}: {len(response)} chars ({tools_token_count(response, args.model)} tokens)")
197	                    sample_data = tools_robust_json_loads(response)
198	                    
199	                    total_tables = len(sample_data.get("tables", []))
200	                    total_inserts = sum(
201	                        len(table.get("insert_statements", [])) 
202	                        for table in sample_data.get("tables", [])
203	                    )
204	                    
205	                    logger.info(f"Generated {total_tables} tables with {total_inserts} INSERT statements")
206	                    
207	                    db_filename = f"{normalize_scenario_name(scenario_name)}.db"
208	                    db_path = f"{args.database_dir}/{db_filename}"
209	                    
210	                    # reset the database before inserting new data
211	                    create_sqlite_database(scenario_name, db_schemas_data[normalize_scenario_name(scenario_name)]["db_schema"], args.database_dir)
212	                    successful, failed, error_msg = execute_sample_data(db_path, sample_data, scenario_name)
213	                    
214	                    total_statements = successful + failed
215	                    if total_statements > 0:
216	                        error_ratio = failed / total_statements
217	                    else:
218	                        error_ratio = 1.0
219	                    
220	                    if error_ratio > error_threshold:
221	                        logger.warning(f"Error ratio too high for {scenario_name}: {failed} / {total_statements} ={error_ratio:.2%} > {error_threshold}, scheduling retry...")
222	                    else:
223	                        result = {
224	                            "scenario": scenario_name,
225	                            "tables_count": total_tables,
226	                            "inserts_count": total_inserts,
227	                            "sample_data": sample_data
228	                        }
229	                        results.append(result)
230	                        total_successful += successful
231	                        total_failed += failed
232	                        logger.success(f"{scenario_name}: Successfully processed with {error_ratio:.2%} error rate")
233	                        continue
234	                    
235	                except Exception as e:
236	                    error_msg = f"Failed to parse or process sample data: {str(e)}"
237	                    logger.error(f"Failed to process sample data for {scenario_name}: {e}")
238	                    logger.error(f"Response preview: {response[:200]}...")
239	                    import traceback
240	                    logger.error(traceback.format_exc())
241	            
242	            
243	            temp = normalize_scenario_name(scenario_name)
244	            if temp not in history_data_messages:
245	                history_data_messages[temp] = []
246	            
247	            failed_result = {
248	                "scenario": scenario_name,
249	                "tables_count": total_tables,
250	                "inserts_count": total_inserts,
251	                "sample_data": sample_data,
252	            }
253	            history_data_messages[temp].append(
254	                (error_ratio, failed_result)
255	            )
256	
257	            if attempt < max_retries:
258	                
259	                if temp not in history_error_messages:
260	                    history_error_messages[temp] = set()
261	                history_error_messages[temp] = history_error_messages[temp].union(error_msg)
262	
263	                combined_error_msg = f"\n{'='*80}\n".join(list(history_error_messages[temp]))
264	                if len(combined_error_msg) > 64_000:
265	                    combined_error_msg = combined_error_msg[-64_000:] + "... (truncated)"
266	
267	                next_items.append(task_item)
268	                next_requests.append((task_item, combined_error_msg))
269	            else:
270	                min_error, min_error_result = sorted(history_data_messages[temp], key=lambda x: x[0])[0]
271	                results.append(min_error_result)
272	                logger.error(f"Given up on {scenario_name} after {max_retries+1} attempts. Selecting best result with {min_error_result['inserts_count']} inserts. error_ratio={min_error}")
273	        
274	
275	        summarized_errors = summarize_errors(args, client, [req[1] for req in next_requests])
276	        next_requests = [create_request(req[0], err_msg) for req, err_msg in zip(next_requests, summarized_errors)]
277	        current_items = next_items
278	        current_requests = next_requests
279	    
280	
281	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(args.output), exist_ok=True)
282	    tools_jsonl_save(results, args.output)
283	    
284	    logger.success(f"\n{'='*100}")
285	    logger.success(f"Sample data generation complete!")
286	    logger.info(f"Scenarios processed: {len(results)}/{len(tasks_data)}")
287	    logger.info(f"Total INSERT statements executed: {total_successful}")
288	    
289	    return results
290

292	def run(config: Config):
293	    generate_and_insert_sample_data(config)

import json
import os
from loguru import logger
from dataclasses import dataclass
from awm.core.db import create_sqlite_database
from awm.core.sample import execute_sample_data
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed
from tqdm import tqdm
from awm.tools import tools_jsonl_load, normalize_scenario_name, find_scenario_entry

@dataclass
class Config:
    input_db: str # database schema file
    input_sample: str # sample data file
    database_dir: str = './outputs/databases'
    scenarios: list[str] | None = None

    def pre_process(self):
        assert os.path.exists(self.input_db), f"Database schema file {self.input_db} not found"
        assert os.path.exists(self.input_sample), f"Sample data file {self.input_sample} not found"
        if self.scenarios:
            self.scenarios = {normalize_scenario_name(name) for name in self.scenarios}

def process_schema(schema_item, database_dir, sample_data_dict):
    scenario_name = schema_item["scenario"]
    db_schema = schema_item["db_schema"]

    logger.info(f"resetting database for {scenario_name}")

    db_path, _, _, _ = create_sqlite_database(scenario_name, db_schema, database_dir)

    successful = 0
    failed = 0
    has_error = False

    if scenario_name in sample_data_dict:
        sample_data = sample_data_dict[scenario_name]
        try:
            successful, failed, _ = execute_sample_data(db_path, sample_data, scenario_name)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error executing sample data for {scenario_name}: {e}")
            has_error = True

        if failed > 0:
            has_error = True
    else:
        has_error = True
        logger.error(f"No sample data found for {scenario_name}")

    return scenario_name, successful, failed, has_error


def reset_single_database(
    input_db: str,
    input_sample: str,
    scenario: str,
    database_dir: str = './outputs/databases',
) -> str:
    """Reset the database for a single scenario.

    Loads the schema and sample data from JSONL files, creates the SQLite
    database, and populates it.

    Args:
        input_db: path to gen_db.jsonl
        input_sample: path to gen_sample.jsonl
        scenario: scenario name (will be normalized)
        database_dir: directory to write the .db file into

    Returns:
        The path to the created database file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if the scenario is not found in the data files.
        RuntimeError: if the database creation fails.
    """
    scenario_norm = normalize_scenario_name(scenario)
    os.makedirs(database_dir, exist_ok=True)

    db_schemas_data = tools_jsonl_load(input_db)
    schema_item = find_scenario_entry(db_schemas_data, scenario_norm)
    if not schema_item:
        raise ValueError(f"Scenario '{scenario}' not found in {input_db}")

    sample_data_list = tools_jsonl_load(input_sample)
    sample_item = find_scenario_entry(sample_data_list, scenario_norm)
    if not sample_item:
        raise ValueError(f"Scenario '{scenario}' not found in {input_sample}")

    sample_data_dict = {sample_item["scenario"]: sample_item["sample_data"]}
    _, successful, failed, has_error = process_schema(schema_item, database_dir, sample_data_dict)

    db_path = os.path.join(database_dir, f"{scenario_norm}.db")
    if not os.path.exists(db_path):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Database file not created: {db_path}")

    if has_error:
        logger.warning(f"Database for {scenario} created with errors (successful={successful}, failed={failed})")

    return db_path

def reset_all_databases(
    input_db: str,
    input_sample: str,
    database_dir: str = './outputs/databases',
    scenarios: set[str] | None = None,
):


    logger.info("="*100)
    logger.info("starting database reset")
    logger.info("="*100)
    
    db_schemas_data = tools_jsonl_load(input_db)
    sample_data_list = tools_jsonl_load(input_sample)

    if scenarios:
        db_schemas_data = [item for item in db_schemas_data if normalize_scenario_name(item["scenario"]) in scenarios]
        sample_data_list = [item for item in sample_data_list if normalize_scenario_name(item["scenario"]) in scenarios]
        logger.info(f"Resetting databases for {len(scenarios)} scenarios: {scenarios}")
    
    sample_data_dict = {item["scenario"]: item["sample_data"] for item in sample_data_list}
    
    total_successful = 0
    total_failed = 0
    no_error_scenarios = []
    error_scenarios = []
    
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(os.cpu_count() or 4, len(db_schemas_data), 64)) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(process_schema, schema_item, database_dir, sample_data_dict) for schema_item in db_schemas_data]
        for future in tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures), desc="Resetting databases"):
            scenario_name, successful, failed, has_error = future.result()
            total_successful += successful
            total_failed += failed
            if has_error:
                error_scenarios.append(scenario_name)
            else:
                no_error_scenarios.append(scenario_name)
    
    
    logger.info(f"="*100)
    logger.info(f"Database reset done! Total/Success/Has_Errors = {len(db_schemas_data)}/{total_successful}/{total_failed}")
    logger.info(f"Scenarios error free: {len(no_error_scenarios)}\n{no_error_scenarios}")
    logger.info(f"Scenarios with errors: {len(error_scenarios)}\n{error_scenarios}")


def run(config: Config):
    reset_all_databases(config.input_db, config.input_sample, config.database_dir, config.scenarios)

    # Helper to safely query database

        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:

    # Check if final_answer exists
    if not final_answer or not isinstance(final_answer, str) or len(final_answer.strip()) == 0:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Query the database to get expected messages
    # Messages for live_event_id=990, timestamp >= '2026-01-02 18:00:00' AND timestamp < '2026-01-02 19:00:00'
    # AND (moderation_flags IS NULL OR moderation_flags NOT LIKE '%banned_word%')
    query = """
        SELECT id, user_id, message_text, timestamp, moderation_flags
        FROM chat_messages
        WHERE live_event_id = 990
        AND timestamp >= '2026-01-02 18:00:00'
        AND timestamp < '2026-01-02 19:00:00'
        AND (moderation_flags IS NULL OR moderation_flags NOT LIKE '%banned_word%')

    """

    found_count = 0
    for text in expected_texts:
        # Escape special regex characters in message text
        escaped_text = re.escape(text)
        if re.search(escaped_text, final_answer, re.IGNORECASE):
            found_count += 1
    
    # All expected messages should be present

    # Check that excluded messages don't appear (especially banned_word messages)

    timestamp_pattern = r'2026-01-02[T\s](18:[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9])'

        for i in range(len(found_timestamps) - 1):
            if found_timestamps[i] > found_timestamps[i+1]:

    def safe_query(db_path: str, query: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list:

            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:
            return []

    target_vin = '2FMPK4K9XKBB12345'
    expected_old_price = 27995.0
    expected_new_price = 26495.0

    # Check initial state of the vehicle
    initial_vehicle = safe_query(
        initial_db_path,
        "SELECT vin, list_price, status FROM inventory_vehicles WHERE vin = ?",
        (target_vin,)
    )
    
    if not initial_vehicle or len(initial_vehicle) == 0:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    initial_price = initial_vehicle[0][1]
    
    # Verify initial price was 27995.0
    if initial_price != expected_old_price:
        return {"result": "others"}

    # Check final state of the vehicle
    final_vehicle = safe_query(
        final_db_path,
        "SELECT vin, list_price, status, dealership_id, year, make, model FROM inventory_vehicles WHERE vin = ?",
        (target_vin,)

    if not final_vehicle or len(final_vehicle) == 0:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    final_price = final_vehicle[0][1]
    
    # Verify price was updated to 26495.0
    if final_price != expected_new_price:
        return {"result": "others"}

    # Get initial notes count for this VIN
    initial_notes = safe_query(
        initial_db_path,
        "SELECT id, note FROM inventory_vehicle_notes WHERE vin = ?",
        (target_vin,)
    )
    initial_note_ids = set(row[0] for row in initial_notes)

    # Get final notes for this VIN
    final_notes = safe_query(
        final_db_path,
        "SELECT id, note FROM inventory_vehicle_notes WHERE vin = ?",
        (target_vin,)
    )
    
    if not final_notes or len(final_notes) == 0:
        return {"result": "others"}

    # Find new notes (notes that exist in final but not in initial)
    new_notes = []
    for note_id, note_text in final_notes:
        if note_id not in initial_note_ids:
            new_notes.append(note_text)

    # Verify at least one new note was added
    if len(new_notes) == 0:
        return {"result": "others"}

    # Check if any new note mentions weekend promotional discount
    # Look for keywords: weekend, promotional, discount, promo
    discount_note_found = False
    for note in new_notes:
        if note:
            note_lower = note.lower()
            # Check for weekend AND (promotional OR promo OR discount)
            has_weekend = 'weekend' in note_lower
            has_discount_term = ('discount' in note_lower or 'promotional' in note_lower or 'promo' in note_lower)

        return {"result": "others"}

    # All checks passed

def verify_task_completion(initial_db_path: str, final_db_path: str, final_answer: str | None = None) -> dict:
    import sqlite3
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta

    def safe_query(db_path: str, query: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list:
        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:
            return []

    # Get the relevant shift assignments (shifts 5004, 5005, 5006 on 2025-02-01 between 9:00-12:00)
    # These are assignment IDs: 10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006
    target_assignment_ids = [10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006]
    
    # Get shift details for validation
    shifts_query = """
        SELECT sa.id, s.start_time, s.end_time, s.opportunity_id
        FROM shift_assignments sa
        JOIN shifts s ON sa.shift_id = s.id
        WHERE sa.id IN (10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006)
    """
    
    shifts_data = safe_query(final_db_path, shifts_query)
    if len(shifts_data) != 6:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Create a mapping of assignment_id to (start_time, end_time)
    shift_times = {}
    for row in shifts_data:
        assignment_id, start_time, end_time, opp_id = row
        shift_times[assignment_id] = (start_time, end_time)
    
    # Get attendance records for these assignments from final database
    attendance_query = """
        SELECT shift_assignment_id, check_in_time, check_out_time, volunteer_hours, attendance_flag
        FROM attendance_records
        WHERE shift_assignment_id IN (10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006)
    """
    
    attendance_records = safe_query(final_db_path, attendance_query)
    
    if len(attendance_records) != 6:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Validate each attendance record
    for record in attendance_records:
        assignment_id, check_in_time, check_out_time, volunteer_hours, attendance_flag = record
        
        if assignment_id not in shift_times:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        start_time_str, end_time_str = shift_times[assignment_id]
        
        # Parse datetime strings
        try:
            start_time = datetime.strptime(start_time_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
            end_time = datetime.strptime(end_time_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        except:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Check for noshow case
        if check_in_time is None and check_out_time is None:

            if volunteer_hours not in [0.0, 0, None]:

        # If there's a check_in, validate times

        try:

        except:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Verify check_in_time equals start_time

        # Verify check_out_time equals end_time

            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Calculate expected volunteer hours

        expected_hours = time_diff.total_seconds() / 3600.0

        # So there should be no 'late' flags unless the volunteer actually came late
        # Re-reading: "check_ins at their scheduled start_time" means we set check_in to the shift start time
        # This means check_in_time = start_time for everyone who showed up
        # So late flag logic: if actual arrival > start + 10min, but we're setting check_in to start_time
        # This is ambiguous. Let me re-read the task.

        # Let me go with: if check_in_time = start_time, flag should be 'on_time'

        metric_pattern = metric.replace('_', '[_ -]?')
        if re.search(metric_pattern, final_answer_lower):
            metrics_found += 1
    
    if metrics_found < 3:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 2: City Auto Group dealerships must be mentioned
    city_auto_dealerships = [
        'city auto',
        'main rooftop',
        'northside',
        'downtown',
        'subaru east'
    ]
    dealership_mentions = sum(1 for d in city_auto_dealerships if d in final_answer_lower)
    if dealership_mentions < 2:  # At least 2 dealership references
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 3: Vehicle models should be present (per model breakdown)

        r'\$[\d,]+',   # Dollar amounts
        r'\d+\s*%'     # Percentages with space
    ]
    numeric_matches = 0
    for pattern in numeric_patterns:
        numeric_matches += len(re.findall(pattern, final_answer))
    
    if numeric_matches < 5:  # Should have multiple numeric values in a report
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 5: Date range should be referenced
    date_patterns = [
        r'2024[-/]07[-/]01',
        r'2024[-/]12[-/]31',
        r'july\s+2024',
        r'december\s+2024',
        r'2024-07',
        r'2024-12'
    ]
    date_found = any(re.search(pattern, final_answer_lower) for pattern in date_patterns)
    
    # Check 6: Sorting indication - look for phrases suggesting sorted by gross profit
    sorting_indicators = [
        'sorted by.*gross.*profit',
        'highest.*gross.*profit',
        'descending.*gross.*profit',
        'gross.*profit.*first',
        'top.*gross.*profit'
    ]
    sorted_mentioned = any(re.search(indicator, final_answer_lower) for indicator in sorting_indicators)
    
    # Check 7: Report structure - should have tabular or structured data
    # Look for common report formatting indicators
    structure_indicators = [
        r'dealership.*model',
        r'model.*dealership',
        r'\|.*\|',  # Table pipes
        r'[-]{3,}',  # Table separators
        r'\n\s*\n'  # Multiple line breaks suggesting sections
    ]
    has_structure = any(re.search(indicator, final_answer, re.IGNORECASE) for indicator in structure_indicators)
    
    # Check 8: Per dealership AND per model breakdown
    # Look for patterns suggesting hierarchical or grouped data
    breakdown_patterns = [
        r'per\s+dealership',
        r'per\s+model',
        r'by\s+dealership',
        r'by\s+model',
        r'each\s+dealership',
        r'each\s+model'
    ]
    breakdown_mentions = sum(1 for pattern in breakdown_patterns if re.search(pattern, final_answer_lower))
    
    # Final decision: All critical checks must pass
    critical_checks_passed = (
        metrics_found == 3 and  # All three metrics present
        dealership_mentions >= 2 and  # City Auto dealerships mentioned
        model_mentions >= 1 and  # Models mentioned
        numeric_matches >= 5 and  # Sufficient numeric data
        (date_found or '2024' in final_answer)  # Date range referenced

        has_structure or  # Report has structure

        sorted_mentioned  # Sorting mentioned
    )
    
    if critical_checks_passed and confidence_checks:
        return {"result": "complete"}
    
    return {"result": "others"}

        try:

            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results

CREATE TABLE bookings (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sitter_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    service_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('requested','confirmed','declined','cancelled','completed')),
    start_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
    end_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
    zip_code TEXT NOT NULL,
    special_notes TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES users(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (sitter_id) REFERENCES sitters(id)
);
CREATE TABLE booking_items (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    booking_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    item_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    quantity REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    unit TEXT,
    rate REAL NOT NULL,
    amount REAL NOT NULL,
    metadata TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE TABLE payouts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sitter_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    total_amount REAL NOT NULL,
    total_platform_fees REAL NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','paid','failed')),
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (sitter_id) REFERENCES sitters(id)
);
CREATE TABLE payout_items (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    payout_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    booking_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sitter_earnings REAL NOT NULL,
    platform_fees REAL NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (payout_id) REFERENCES payouts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id)
);

## Main findings

- The 128 held-out rows in `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/verl/test.parquet` all resolve to a verifier by **normalized scenario name plus zero-based `task_idx`**. All 128 have a match, and every selected verifier’s task text exactly matches the parquet task.
- Lookup is **first matching JSONL row wins**, not positional and not last-row-wins.
- The verifier file contains **10,010 rows but only 10,000 unique keys**. Ten keys are duplicated with different verifier code. None is held out; all ten occur in training. The appended rows 10001–10010 are unreachable under the current runtime lookup.
- Recorded validation logs show repeated initial-database sample insertion failures. These are warnings only; episodes and verification continue with partially initialized databases.
- Pure-code verifier execution errors, ordinary unsuccessful verification, and environment failures can all collapse to scalar reward `0.0`, with no persistent pure-code verifier trace or validation rollout dump.

## Held-out selection and execution

`/workspace/idea_source/examples/data_preprocess/preprocess_awm_dataset.py`:

- Lines 12–22 flatten `gen_tasks.jsonl` in file order and assign zero-based `task_idx` using `enumerate(row["tasks"])`.
- Lines 40–48 shuffle all 10,000 tasks with `random.Random(20260910)` and take the first 128 as `test`.
- Lines 25–33 store the key in `env_kwargs`; `extra_info.index` is only the shuffled row index, not the verifier index.

I reproduced the shuffle in memory: the current 128 test rows match exactly, in the same order. The remaining train set has 9,872 rows, with no key overlap.

Relevant recorded Hydra values in `/workspace/config/.hydra/config.yaml`:

- `data.val_files=/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/verl/test.parquet`: line 5.
- `data.val_batch_size=8`: line 11.
- `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1`, temperature `0.4`, sampling enabled: lines 152–157.
- `env.max_steps=20`: line 344.
- `env.awm.reward_mode=code`: line 364.
- `trainer.val_before_train=false`, `test_freq=50`, `total_training_steps=200`: lines 328–330 and 314.

The validation dataloader is unshuffled and does not drop rows, giving 16 batches of eight: `/workspace/idea_source/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:1256-1267`. Validation repeats each row only by `val_kwargs.n=1`: lines 1762–1766. Validation does **not** apply training’s `env.rollout.n=8` repetition because repetition is conditional on `is_train`: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/multi_turn_rollout/rollout_loop.py:1010-1012`.

Consequently, each validation sweep runs one episode for each of the 128 rows. With the recorded schedule, sweeps occur at steps 50, 100, 150, and 200; there is no initial validation: `/workspace/idea_source/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:3040-3046,3410-3416`.

At episode reset:

1. `env_kwargs` is passed unchanged to the environment: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/multi_turn_rollout/rollout_loop.py:726-733`.
2. The bridge converts `scenario` to `str` and `task_idx` to `int`: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py:170-173`.
3. Code mode loads `gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`: bridge lines 109–110.
4. Verifier selection occurs at bridge line 217 through `find_scenario_entry`.
5. `/workspace/awm_source/awm/tools.py:456-472` scans from the beginning and returns the first entry whose normalized scenario matches and whose `task_idx` is exactly equal.

The task string is not part of selection. All scenario names in this file are already in normalized form.

### Do not use positional arithmetic

The first 10,000 verifier rows are **not** positionally aligned with `10 * gen_tasks_scenario_row + task_idx`. For example:

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_tasks.jsonl:6` is `social_networking_5`; its task 9 would positionally imply verifier line 60.
- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl:60` is instead `social_media_4`, task 0.

Runtime key lookup handles this correctly.

## Verifier-health flags

### 1. Partial database initialization is allowed to proceed

`/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/sample.py:89-108` catches individual SQL insertion errors, continues executing subsequent statements, and commits the successful subset.

`/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/reset.py:91-100` discards the returned detailed error set, logs only a warning when failures occurred, and returns the database path. The bridge then starts the environment and verifier normally.

The historical validation bridge log:

`/workspace/logs/awm_runtime/bridge_3339424_139533888048880.log`

contains:

- 512 MCP server starts, consistent with four 128-episode validation sweeps.
- 124 initialization-warning events: the same 31 held-out episode initializations per sweep.
- 30 distinct affected scenarios; `marketplace_6` accounts for two held-out tasks.
- 192 failed insertion statements per sweep, 768 overall.

Examples include:

- `booking_scheduling_3`: log line 5, one failed insertion.
- `payments_1`: line 20, six failures.
- `q_a_forum_1`: line 28, 38 failures.
- `professional_networking_1`: line 3697, 15 failures.
- `booking_reservations_18`: line 3705, 12 failures.

Thus some verifier comparisons run against databases missing part of their specified initial sample state.

### 2. Scalar zero reward conflates verifier failure with ordinary non-completion

Pure-code execution exceptions are caught and returned as verifier errors at `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/verify.py:192-193`; `run_verifier` converts these to `judge_error` at lines 218–222.

The bridge maps all of the following to `0.0`:

- Pure-code `others`.
- `judge_error`.
- `environment_error`.
- Unknown reward types via the fallback.

See `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py:21-40,279-280`. Startup failures also produce zero reward and `environment_error`: bridge lines 325–331.

For terminal shaping, a verifier `complete` reached without a final answer becomes `0.5`, while `others` remains zero: bridge lines 299–323.

Therefore reward/score alone cannot distinguish an unhealthy verifier from an unsuccessful agent or broken environment.

### 3. Pure-code verifier diagnostics are not persisted by the training/validation path

The bridge returns `reward_type` and `verify_result` in environment info: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/envs.py:101-109`. However:

- `EpisodeRewardManager` returns an empty `reward_extra_info` dictionary: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/reward_manager/episode.py:90-94`.
- Validation metrics aggregate only reward, tool-call count, and success, not `reward_type`: `/workspace/idea_source/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:1847-1892`.
- The rollout dump allowlist omits `reward_type` and `verify_result`: ray trainer lines 3386–3400.
- Only training rollouts are dumped through that path. Recorded config has `trainer.validation_data_dir=null` and `log_val_generations=0`: `/workspace/config/.hydra/config.yaml:320-322`.
- `_record_judge` is called only in SQL mode, so code mode gets no `llm_judge.jsonl` verifier trace: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py:443-452`.

The bridge logs capture subprocess stderr, but pure-code verifier exceptions are returned rather than logged. Their absence from bridge logs therefore does not establish verifier health.

### 4. No pure-code verifier timeout or process isolation

`execute_code_verifier` directly executes generated code and calls the function in the bridge process:

- `exec(verifier_code, namespace)`: `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/verify.py:175`.
- Verifier invocation: line 181.
- Synchronous call from the async bridge: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py:259-263`.

`tool_timeout` governs MCP calls and `judge_timeout` governs hosted SQL judging; neither bounds pure-code verifier execution. A blocking verifier can therefore block the bridge’s event loop and all sessions managed by that bridge.

### 5. Packaged checks do not cover these mapping/health conditions

`/workspace/reproduce.py:117-153` reads the verifier JSONL but checks only scenario presence. It does not check:

- `(scenario, task_idx)` verifier coverage.
- Duplicate keys.
- Verifier task-text alignment.
- Verifier execution.

The `--smoke` selection at `/workspace/reproduce.py:162-170` scans the training rows first and selects only previously unseen scenarios from later splits. The current train split covers all 1,000 scenarios, so **zero held-out rows are selected**. It instead attempts one training task per scenario—1,000 environment sessions—rather than serving as a focused held-out verifier check.

### 6. Code mode does not use the configured hosted judge

The recorded invalid judge URL and `EMPTY` key at `/workspace/config/.hydra/config.yaml:364-369` do not affect this run because `reward_mode=code`. The bridge selects the pure-code file and invokes the hosted judge only when mode is `sql`: `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py:109-110,265-275`.

`/workspace/reproduce.py:95-102` likewise strips judge credentials in code mode and only requires them for SQL mode.

### 7. Runtime interpreters are external prerequisites

The recorded `/workspace/awm_source/.venv/bin/python` is absent from the packaged tree. The wrapper defaults to `/opt/awm/bin/python`, and `/workspace/run_local.sh` defaults to `/opt/idea/bin/python`; neither default exists in the current environment. The scripts are designed to fail early unless `TRAIN_PYTHON`/`AWM_PYTHON` or runtime-local paths are provisioned. No training was launched.

steps.message:
Audited all 32 held-out episodes against `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`. Strong defects were found in 16 verifiers. No broad tests were run.

## Highest priority

1. **Episode 105 — JSONL row 6243 — `marketplace_6`, task_idx 3: wrong sitter ID rejects the correct completion.**
   - Faulty condition: `AND sitter_id = 2`
   - The task explicitly targets `sitter_profile_id 452`. The schema’s `bookings.sitter_id` references `sitters(id)`, and the sample contains distinct sitter rows with IDs **2** and **452**.
   - Therefore a correct booking targeting sitter 452 is rejected, while an otherwise matching booking for sitter 2 can be accepted.

2. **Episode 121 — JSONL row 6169 — `task_management_17`, task_idx 6: contradicts actual checkout and late-flag requirements.**
   - Faulty conditions:
     - `if check_out_dt != end_time: return {"result": "others"}`
     - `if check_in_dt != start_time: return {"result": "others"}`
     - A subsequent block rejects `attendance_flag='late'` whenever check-in equals shift start.

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The user’s original request was to review the staged post-training experiment in `/workspace`, determine whether it is healthy, and repair any defect in the staged workspace. The audit was to cover source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Unusual settings were not to be treated as causal without observed behavioral evidence. Held-out evaluation had to be considered alongside rollout, truncation, runtime, optimization, and training signals; increasing training reward with decreasing held-out accuracy is explicitly a warning.

The exact operational constraints are:

- “If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not launch training.**”
- “Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach mechanism.”
- “Cheap, non-training checks are fine.”
- Submit `/workspace/report.md`; a missing or empty report scores zero.
- The report must contain:
  1. Root cause, with workspace evidence connecting the defect to observed behavior.
  2. Every changed file and what changed.
  3. Expected effect and direction.
- The system will not rerun training or use an LLM judge. It will replay held-out episodes through rules selected from:
  `data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`
- Incomplete trajectories must be judged incomplete; correct completions of the same tasks must remain complete.
- “The rule file must be repaired in place: every original entry must remain present and parseable, and a file that was wholesale-replaced, truncated, or corrupted makes the run ungradeable and scores 0.”
- “Do not modify the preserved evidence under `logs/`, and do not modify any evaluation, oracle, or verifier file. Otherwise the run is scored 0.”
  
The designated JSONL rule file is therefore the allowed repair target; verifier implementation/source files and preserved evaluation evidence are not to be changed.

The second user message requested this text-only compaction summary and prohibited further tool calls for that turn.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

- AgentWorldModel-1K synthetic SQL-backed MCP environments.
- Pure-code verifiers with the common signature:
  ```python
  def verify_task_completion(
      initial_db_path: str,
      final_db_path: str,
      final_answer: str | None = None
  ) -> dict:
  ```
  Successful verdicts use `{"result": "complete"}`; unsuccessful verdicts generally use `{"result": "others"}`.
- Verifier selection by normalized scenario name and zero-based `task_idx`.
- First-match-wins JSONL lookup, not positional or last-match lookup.
- Held-out split of 128 tasks, training split of 9,872 tasks, disjoint by `(scenario, task_idx)`.
- SQLite initial/final state comparison and final-answer validation.
- No-op replay: using identical logical initial/final states to expose false-positive completion.
- New-record/newness checks versus update/change checks.
- Avoiding false-negative repairs for correct completions.
- Hydra-effective configuration, PPO training, MCP rollouts, code reward mode.
- Frozen W&B metrics and AWM runtime logs.
- Lightweight `python -I` checks; no model inference or training.
- Public upstream reference comparison using SHA-256.

3. Files and Code Sections:

- `/workspace/reproduce.py`
  - Read in full.
  - Prepares relocated configs, checks inputs, optionally performs smoke tests or launches training.
  - `check()` verifies task alignment and split disjointness but only checks scenario presence in verifier data, not exact verifier-key coverage, duplicate keys, or verifier execution.
  - Its smoke selection scans training rows first; because training covers all 1,000 scenarios, it does not provide focused held-out rule coverage.
  - No edits made.

- `/workspace/run_local.sh`
  - Read; wraps `reproduce.py` with an explicitly provisioned interpreter.
  - No edits made.

- `/workspace/config/.hydra/config.yaml`
  - Effective code-reward configuration:
    - `data.val_files=/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/verl/test.parquet`
    - `data.val_batch_size=8`
    - `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1`
    - validation temperature `0.4`
    - `env.max_steps=20`
    - `env.awm.reward_mode=code`
    - `trainer.val_before_train=false`
    - `trainer.test_freq=50`
    - `trainer.total_training_steps=200`
    - `trainer.validation_data_dir=null`
    - `trainer.log_val_generations=0`
  - The invalid hosted-judge URL and empty judge key are not causal in code mode.
  - No edits made.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`
  - Primary repair target; currently unchanged.
  - 10,010 JSONL rows, 10,000 unique task keys, ten duplicate keys.
  - All rows have `scenario`, `task_idx`, `task`, and `verification`; `verification` contains `code` and `raw_response`.
  - The original 10,000 rows generally have empty `raw_response`; the ten appended alternatives have populated responses.
  - No missing task keys and no task-text mismatches against `gen_tasks.jsonl`.
  - No held-out key is duplicated.
  - Two original training rules have Python syntax errors (`q_a_knowledge_base_1`, task 1, row index 9996; `ticketing_and_access_management_1`, task 5, row index 9998), but these are not held out. Their appended alternatives are unreachable under first-match lookup. This is not the current held-out repair focus.
  - SHA-256:
    `2de0b668bd0c6b37a033dda7d697bcd8ddc3bf5b0c9bf83fbd691fbd2c3827f7`.

- `/tmp/awm-reference-YX9PcP/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`
  - Downloaded public upstream reference into its own scratch directory.
  - Source:
    `https://hf-mirror.com/datasets/locaszzz/IDEA_training_data/resolve/main/runtime/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`
  - Upstream commit reported by headers:
    `e49176428defd16416d9f5b11ab7eaca170d5732`.
  - Byte-identical to the staged target, proving the target was not locally altered from that reference.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/verl/test.parquet`
  - Contains 128 held-out tasks.
  - Each row’s `env_kwargs` supplies `scenario`, `task_idx`, and `task`.
  - No overlap with training keys.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_tasks.jsonl`
  - Used to confirm all verifier keys and task strings.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_db.jsonl`
  - Contains per-scenario table DDL and indexes.
  - Used by the no-op harness to reconstruct initial databases.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_sample.jsonl`
  - Contains per-table insert statements.
  - Many target states already exist in the sample data, which is why final-state-only rules can accept no-op episodes.

- `/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_envs.jsonl`
  - Environment implementations for the relevant scenarios.
  - Most recently used to extract behavior for:
    - `productivity_assistant_1`
    - `booking_reservations_24`
    - `recruiting_platform_1`
    - `booking_platform_1`

- `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/db.py`
  - `create_sqlite_database()` executes DDL/index/example statements and commits.
  - Read to make the scratch database construction match AWM behavior.

- `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/sample.py`
  - `execute_sample_data()` enables foreign keys, executes inserts individually, catches insertion errors, continues, and commits successful rows.
  - Partial initialization is therefore allowed.

- `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/reset.py`
  - Resets databases and logs warnings on sample insertion failures but returns the partially initialized database.
  - Used to validate the no-op harness’s reconstruction approach.

- `/workspace/idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py`
  - Source-tracing agent established:
    - Code mode loads `gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`.
    - Scenario/task index are converted to `str`/`int`.
    - Verifier selection calls `find_scenario_entry`.
    - Pure-code `others`, judge errors, and environment errors collapse to scalar zero reward.
    - A verifier `complete` reached without a final answer can become `0.5` through terminal shaping.
  - No edits made.

- `/workspace/awm_source/awm/tools.py`
  - `find_scenario_entry` scans from the beginning and returns the first normalized scenario/task-index match.
  - This resolves the duplicate-rule question: appended alternatives are not selected.

- `/workspace/awm_source/awm/core/verify.py`
  - Executes verifier code directly with `exec` and calls it synchronously.
  - No process isolation or pure-code verifier timeout.
  - Not modified.

- `/workspace/idea_source/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`
  - Source agent confirmed validation dataloader order, one episode per held-out row, validation schedule, and aggregate-only validation metrics.
  - Rollout dump allowlist omits `reward_type` and `verify_result`; validation rollout dump is not configured.

- `/workspace/logs/wandb/run-20261011_112547-wszt4s3y/history.jsonl`
  - Preserved; not modified.
  - Validation metrics:
    ```text
    step 50:
      val/success_rate = 0.390625
      val/agent_world_model/test_score = 0.38571428571428573
    step 100:
      val/success_rate = 0.390625
      val/agent_world_model/test_score = 0.3797071129707113
    step 150:
      val/success_rate = 0.3359375
      val/agent_world_model/test_score = 0.3464052287581699
    ```
  - Training `critic/score/mean` starts around `0.02455`, reaches values above `0.6`, and ends with fluctuating values such as `0.47115`, `0.48307`, `0.29`, and `0.37402`.
  - Response and prompt clipping exist but were not connected to the verifier false positives.

- `/workspace/logs/awm_runtime/bridge_3339424_139533888048880.log`
  - Preserved; not modified.
  - Contains 512 MCP starts, consistent with four 128-episode validation sweeps.
  - Source agent counted 124 initialization-warning events, corresponding to 31 warnings per sweep, affecting 30 distinct scenarios; `marketplace_6` has two held-out tasks.
  - There are 192 failed sample insertions per sweep.
  - These warnings are relevant context but have not been shown to cause the specific no-op false positives.

- `/workspace/logs/rollouts/*.jsonl`
  - Inspected record structure and sampled outcomes.
  - Training rollout records contain `input`, `output`, `score`, step/sample/rollout identifiers, observations, and action validity.
  - They do not supply a held-out per-rule verifier trace.

- `/tmp/awm-analysis-FY8vek/audit_noop.py`
  - Created scratch harness; no workspace source changes.
  - Loads held-out parquet rows, reconstructs scenario DBs, executes each selected verifier, and tests four answers:
    ```python
    answers = [
        ('none', None),
        ('empty', ''),
        ('generic',
         'I have completed the requested task and verified all of the requested details. '
         'Here are the complete results for your request.'),
        ('task_restatement', env['task']),
    ]
    ```
  - Core replay:
    ```python
    verdict = fn(str(db_path), str(db_path), answer)
    ```
  - Uses a five-second alarm per rule and writes structured results.
  - No model inference or training.

- `/tmp/awm-analysis-FY8vek/noop_results.json`
  - 512 replay results: 128 rules × four answer variants.
  - Source of the 23 no-op/task-restatement false-positive findings.

- `/tmp/awm-analysis-FY8vek/noop_complete_rules.txt`
  - Contains the full task and verifier code for the 22 rules that returned complete with `final_answer=None`.
  - Used for detailed audit.

- `/tmp/awm-analysis-FY8vek/env_snippets.txt`
  - Most recently created file.
  - Contains environment code snippets concerning:
    - sales analysis tasks/predictors,
    - event-type reminders,
    - event RSVPs/job preferences,
    - crew assignments/duty-time behavior.
  - It had not yet been read when the summary was requested.

4. Errors and Fixes:

- Initial `find /workspace ...` returned only the symlink.
  - Fixed by using `ls -la /workspace/` and `find -L /workspace ...`.

- Attempting to list `/user/user1/harbor-runs/a90cc070fa7a/` returned permission denied.
  - This was not needed for the repair; work continued through `/workspace`.

- First no-op harness run failed at test row 17:
  ```text
  TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable PosixPath object
  ```
  - The cached-database path returned only `path`, while new databases returned `(path, db_info)`.
  - Fixed the early return to:
    ```python
    if path.exists():
        return path, {'cached': True}
    ```
  - Rerun completed all 512 checks.

- Direct HTTPS access to `huggingface.co` failed with TLS unexpected EOF through the configured proxy.
  - Used the public `hf-mirror.com` endpoint instead.
  - Download succeeded and established byte equality with the staged file.
  - `raw.githubusercontent.com` was also unreachable, but was unnecessary.

- Several large inspection outputs exceeded display limits and were persisted by the harness.
  - This did not block analysis; subsequent checks printed focused summaries instead.

- AST parsing emitted many `SyntaxWarning` messages for invalid escape sequences in generated verifier code.
  - These were mostly nonfatal upstream code-quality issues.
  - Only two actual Python syntax failures were found, both in non-held-out training rules.
  - All JSONL entries remained JSON-parseable.

- No user feedback corrected the technical approach. The final user message only changed the immediate output mode to a text-only summary.

5. Problem Solving:

Solved or strongly established:

- The experiment is unhealthy at the reward-verification layer: concrete no-op states are judged complete.
- The held-out metric trend is unfavorable, with success falling at step 150 while training reward remains comparatively high.
- The selected held-out rules are unambiguous: exact scenario/task-index lookup, first match, no duplicate held-out keys.
- The ten duplicate rules are not the cause of the held-out failures.
- The target file was not locally mutated relative to its upstream reference; the defects are inherited.
- Partial sample initialization and absent verifier diagnostics make metric interpretation harder, but neither has been used as an unsupported explanation for the no-op verdicts.
- A direct, reproducible false-positive mechanism exists: pre-existing sample rows satisfy final-state-only verifier checks without any agent action.

The 22 rules that returned `complete` with identical initial/final DBs and `final_answer=None` are listed below as `(held-out test row, zero-based verifier JSONL row, scenario, task_idx)`:

```text
(0,   1860, booking_scheduling_3, 8)
(6,   118,  productivity_assistant_1, 1)
(8,   3041, property_management_11, 0)
(22,  609,  booking_reservations_24, 7)
(23,  4579, e_commerce_35, 5)
(24,  6769, event_management_8, 8)
(39,  7157, recruiting_platform_1, 5)
(40,  9515, crm_9, 6)
(42,  9301, stock_trading_2, 0)
(47,  2720, learning_management_system_6, 4)
(53,  8055, booking_scheduling_7, 0)
(63,  5173, document_management_4, 8)
(71,  5066, wishlist_management_5, 9)
(72,  2932, productivity_1, 9)
(78,  8335, billing_and_invoicing_3, 4)
(81,  7309, grant_management_1, 8)
(84,  7643, forms_and_survey_platform_1, 0)
(85,  2308, incident_management_1, 5)
(93,  2377, task_management_8, 6)
(99,  9519, volunteer_management_2, 1)
(111, 6133, job_board_3, 9)
(122, 7478, booking_and_scheduling_4, 3)
```

Additional answer-only false positive:

```text
(52, 5953, booking_platform_1, 4)
```

This rule rejected `None`, empty, and generic answers on the no-op DB but accepted the task restatement.

Two cases require caution rather than automatic patching:

- `event_management_8`, task 8, test row 24:
  The rule computes attendees needing badges. If none need badges, it treats unchanged badge count as complete. That can be a legitimate vacuous completion.
- `task_management_8`, task 6, test row 93:
  The rule computes eligible shifts. If none are eligible and no new assignments were made, it returns complete. That can also be legitimate.

The current strong repair candidate set is therefore the other 20 no-op rules plus `booking_platform_1`, task 4: 21 rules total. This set is still under audit, not yet patched.

Concrete code defects identified include:

- `document_management_4`, task 8, verifier row 5173:
  It queries `initial_docs` and comments that the document should exist in final but not initial, but never enforces that condition.
  ```python
  initial_docs = safe_query(initial_db_path, doc_query)
  final_docs = safe_query(final_db_path, doc_query)
  # ...
  # Missing: reject doc_id already present in initial_docs
  ```
  It also reads initial sections and permissions without using them to establish a delta.

- `forms_and_survey_platform_1`, task 0, verifier row 7643:
  It finds new template IDs but explicitly falls back to accepting a pre-existing template:
  ```python
  if not new_template:
      # Since task says "create a new", we should expect a new template, but let's be flexible
      if len(final_templates) > 0:
          new_template = final_templates[0]
  ```
  This defeats the new-template requirement.

- `grant_management_1`, task 8, verifier row 7309:
  It reads initial progress-report IDs but, when a report already existed, only checks that the final narrative matches the requested narrative. It does not require a new report or an actual update.

- `job_board_3`, task 9, verifier row 6133:
  It excludes only the original listing ID 2875 and never requires the duplicate listing ID to be absent from the initial DB.

- `booking_and_scheduling_4`, task 3, verifier row 7478:
  It reads initial and final appointment states but never requires the scheduled time, status, or metadata to have changed. The already-matching initial appointment therefore passes.

- `recruiting_platform_1`, task 5, verifier row 7157:
  It accepts any matching RSVP where:
  ```python
  student_profile_id in [1, 2, 3, 4]
  ```
  despite the primary student context, and it has no initial/final newness or update check.

- `volunteer_management_2`, task 1, verifier row 9519:
  It validates only final skill, interest, and availability sets, so pre-existing complete sets pass without the requested profile update.

- `booking_platform_1`, task 4, verifier row 5953:
  ```python
  duty_valid = check_duty_hours(all_assignments)
  ```
  is computed but unused. Later:
  ```python
  if has_assignment_info and has_leg_info:
      return {"result": "complete"}
  ```
  Thus duty-limit violations are not enforced, and pre-existing assignments plus answer keywords can pass.

- `productivity_assistant_1`, task 1, verifier row 118:
  It selects any completed `sales_analysis` task and its existing analysis/predictors/recommendations, without requiring a new analysis or a status change.

- `booking_reservations_24`, task 7; `property_management_11`, task 0; `e_commerce_35`, task 5; `crm_9`, task 6; `stock_trading_2`, task 0; `learning_management_system_6`, task 4; `booking_scheduling_7`, task 0; `wishlist_management_5`, task 9; `productivity_1`, task 9; `billing_and_invoicing_3`, task 4; `incident_management_1`, task 5:
  These primarily check final existence and attributes and need task-appropriate new-record or changed-state guards.

A static unused-variable scan also flagged potentially relevant held-out signals, including:
- `initial_docs`, `initial_sections`, `initial_perms` in `document_management_4`.
- `duty_valid` in `booking_platform_1`.
- `all_bookings_valid` in `booking_and_scheduling_14`.
- `has_execution_mention` in `stock_trading_and_brokerage_1`.
- `has_risk_buckets` in `finance_treasury_management_1`.
- Numerous initial-state variables in other rules.
These are audit leads, not all confirmed defects.

Ongoing work:

- Four read-only subset audit agents were still active:
  - held-out rows 0–31,
  - rows 32–63,
  - rows 64–95,
  - rows 96–127.
- Their findings should be incorporated before finalizing the patch.
- Correct-completion regression tests have not yet been written.
- No rule changes have been made.
- The required report has not yet been written.

6. All User Messages:

- Original task message:
  - “Improve the staged experiment.”
  - Review source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs, metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence.
  - Use held-out evidence with rollout, truncation, runtime, optimization, and training signals.
  - Training reward alone does not establish held-out health.
  - Repair defects in `/workspace`.
  - “**Do not launch training.**”
  - “Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach mechanism.”
  - Cheap non-training checks are allowed.
  - Submit `/workspace/report.md` with root cause, changes, and expected effect.
  - The task-specific verifier will replay incomplete and correct held-out episodes using the selected JSONL rule.
  - Every original JSONL entry must remain present and parseable.

CREATE TABLE payouts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payment_account_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    CHECK (status IN ('pending','processing','completed','failed')),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (payment_account_id) REFERENCES payment_accounts(id)
);
CREATE TABLE transactions (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    order_id INTEGER,
    payout_id INTEGER,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    CHECK (type IN ('order_earning','order_refund','payout','adjustment')),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (payout_id) REFERENCES payouts(id)
);

meal_plans CREATE TABLE meal_plans (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  campus_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  price REAL NOT NULL CHECK (price >= 0),
  valid_days TEXT,
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  FOREIGN KEY (campus_id) REFERENCES campuses(id)
);
user_wallets CREATE TABLE user_wallets (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  wallet_balance REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (wallet_balance >= 0),
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
);
user_meal_plans CREATE TABLE user_meal_plans (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  meal_plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  campus_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  purchase_price REAL NOT NULL CHECK (purchase_price >= 0),
  start_date DATE NOT NULL,
  end_date DATE,
  balance_value REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (balance_value >= 0),
  active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (active IN (0,1)),
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (meal_plan_id) REFERENCES meal_plans(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (campus_id) REFERENCES campuses(id)
);
orders CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  dining_location_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  campus_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  fulfillment_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (fulfillment_type IN ('pickup', 'delivery_to_dorm')),
  delivery_address TEXT,
  pickup_window_id INTEGER,
  scheduled_pickup_datetime DATETIME NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('placed', 'in_preparation', 'ready', 'completed', 'canceled')),
  subtotal REAL NOT NULL CHECK (subtotal >= 0),
  tax REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (tax >= 0),
  total REAL NOT NULL CHECK (total >= 0),
  payment_meal_plan_amount REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (payment_meal_plan_amount >= 0),
  payment_wallet_amount REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (payment_wallet_amount >= 0),
  loyalty_points_redeemed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (loyalty_points_redeemed >= 0),
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (dining_location_id) REFERENCES dining_locations(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (campus_id) REFERENCES campuses(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (pickup_window_id) REFERENCES pickup_windows(id)
);

def verify_task_completion(initial_db_path: str, final_db_path: str, final_answer: str | None = None) -> dict:
    import sqlite3
    import re
    from datetime import datetime

    def safe_query(db_path: str, query: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list:
        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:
            return []

    # Get all booking IDs from initial state
    initial_booking_ids = set()
    initial_bookings = safe_query(initial_db_path, "SELECT id FROM bookings", ())
    for row in initial_bookings:
        initial_booking_ids.add(row[0])

    # Get all bookings from final state that match our criteria
    final_bookings_query = """
        SELECT id, owner_id, sitter_id, service_type, status, start_time, end_time, zip_code, special_notes
        FROM bookings
        WHERE owner_id = 1
        AND sitter_id = 2
        AND service_type = 'overnight'
        AND status = 'requested'
        AND zip_code = '10001'
    """
    final_bookings = safe_query(final_db_path, final_bookings_query, ())

    # Find new bookings that weren't in initial state
    new_matching_bookings = []
    for booking in final_bookings:

        start_time_normalized = start_time.replace('T', ' ').strip()
        if not (start_time_normalized == '2025-07-03 19:00:00' or start_time_normalized.startswith('2025-07-03 19:00')):
            continue

        # Verify end_time matches 2025-07-04 08:00
        end_time_normalized = end_time.replace('T', ' ').strip()
        if not (end_time_normalized == '2025-07-04 08:00:00' or end_time_normalized.startswith('2025-07-04 08:00')):
            continue

        # Verify special_notes contains the required text
        if not special_notes:
            continue
        if 'Needs medication at 10pm and 7am' not in special_notes:
            continue

        # Verify pet Buddy (pet_id=1) is linked to this booking
        booking_pets = safe_query(final_db_path, "SELECT pet_id FROM booking_pets WHERE booking_id = ?", (booking_id,))
        pet_ids = [row[0] for row in booking_pets]
        if 1 not in pet_ids:
            continue

        # Verify booking status history exists for this booking with status 'requested'
        status_history = safe_query(final_db_path, 
            "SELECT new_status FROM booking_status_history WHERE booking_id = ? AND new_status = 'requested'",
            (booking_id,))
        if not status_history:
            continue

        # All checks passed for this booking
        return {"result": "complete"}

    # No booking met all criteria
    return {"result": "others"}

TASK: During the 'Saturday Food Pantry' event on 2025-02-01, record check_ins at their scheduled start_time and check_outs at their actual end_time for all volunteers assigned to shifts between 9:00–12:00, calculate their volunteer_hours per shift, and persist attendance_flags 'late' for anyone who checked in more than 10 minutes after shift start and 'noshow' for any assigned volunteer who never checked in.
def verify_task_completion(initial_db_path: str, final_db_path: str, final_answer: str | None = None) -> dict:
    import sqlite3
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta

    def safe_query(db_path: str, query: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list:
        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:
            return []

    # Get the relevant shift assignments (shifts 5004, 5005, 5006 on 2025-02-01 between 9:00-12:00)
    # These are assignment IDs: 10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006
    target_assignment_ids = [10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006]
    
    # Get shift details for validation
    shifts_query = """
        SELECT sa.id, s.start_time, s.end_time, s.opportunity_id
        FROM shift_assignments sa
        JOIN shifts s ON sa.shift_id = s.id
        WHERE sa.id IN (10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006)
    """
    
    shifts_data = safe_query(final_db_path, shifts_query)
    if len(shifts_data) != 6:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Create a mapping of assignment_id to (start_time, end_time)
    shift_times = {}
    for row in shifts_data:
        assignment_id, start_time, end_time, opp_id = row
        shift_times[assignment_id] = (start_time, end_time)
    
    # Get attendance records for these assignments from final database
    attendance_query = """
        SELECT shift_assignment_id, check_in_time, check_out_time, volunteer_hours, attendance_flag
        FROM attendance_records
        WHERE shift_assignment_id IN (10001, 10002, 10003, 10004, 10005, 10006)
    """
    
    attendance_records = safe_query(final_db_path, attendance_query)
    
    if len(attendance_records) != 6:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Validate each attendance record
    for record in attendance_records:
        assignment_id, check_in_time, check_out_time, volunteer_hours, attendance_flag = record
        
        if assignment_id not in shift_times:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        start_time_str, end_time_str = shift_times[assignment_id]
        
        # Parse datetime strings
        try:
            start_time = datetime.strptime(start_time_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
            end_time = datetime.strptime(end_time_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        except:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Check for noshow case
        if check_in_time is None and check_out_time is None:
            if attendance_flag != 'noshow':
                return {"result": "others"}
            if volunteer_hours not in [0.0, 0, None]:
                return {"result": "others"}
            continue
        
        # If there's a check_in, validate times
        if check_in_time is None:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        try:
            check_in_dt = datetime.strptime(check_in_time, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
            check_out_dt = datetime.strptime(check_out_time, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if check_out_time else None
        except:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Verify check_in_time equals start_time
        if check_in_dt != start_time:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Verify check_out_time equals end_time
        if check_out_dt != end_time:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Calculate expected volunteer hours
        time_diff = end_time - start_time
        expected_hours = time_diff.total_seconds() / 3600.0
        
        # Verify volunteer_hours (allow small floating point differences)
        if volunteer_hours is None or abs(volunteer_hours - expected_hours) > 0.01:
            return {"result": "others"}
        
        # Verify attendance_flag
        # If check_in > start_time + 10 minutes, should be 'late'
        # Since check_in_time should equal start_time per task requirements, all should be 'on_time'
        # But task says "record check_ins at their scheduled start_time", meaning we use start_time as check_in
        # So there should be no 'late' flags unless the volunteer actually came late
        # Re-reading: "check_ins at their scheduled start_time" means we set check_in to the shift start time
        # This means check_in_time = start_time for everyone who showed up
        # So late flag logic: if actual arrival > start + 10min, but we're setting check_in to start_time
        # This is ambiguous. Let me re-read the task.
        
        # Task: "record check_ins at their scheduled start_time and check_outs at their actual end_time"
        # This means: check_in_time = shift.start_time, check_out_time = shift.end_time
        # "attendance_flags 'late' for anyone who checked in more than 10 minutes after shift start"
        # But if we're setting check_in_time to start_time, how can they be late?
        # This seems contradictory. Let me interpret: perhaps the system records when they actually arrived,
        # and if that was >10 min late, flag them as 'late', but still record check_in at their actual time?
        
        # Actually, re-reading more carefully: "record check_ins at their scheduled start_time"
        # might mean: record the check_in event at the scheduled time (as the timestamp)
        # But the flag indicates if they were actually late.
        
        # Given the initial data shows some records with check_in != start_time and late flags,
        # I think the intended behavior is: check_in_time should be set to start_time,
        # and if someone didn't show or was late, that's reflected in the flag only.
        
        # But that doesn't make sense either. Let me look at initial data:
        # ID 1: shift 10001, check_in 09:05, shift starts 09:00, flag='late'
        # So check_in_time is when they actually arrived, not the scheduled time.
        
        # Re-reading task again: "record check_ins at their scheduled start_time"
        # I think this means: FOR THOSE WHO SHOWED UP, record their check_in as the shift start_time
        # And check_out as the shift end_time. Then calculate hours and set flags based on
        # whether they would have been late (but we don't have that info if we're setting to start_time).
        
        # This is confusing. Let me try another interpretation:
        # The task wants us to: for all assigned volunteers, create attendance records
        # where check_in = start_time and check_out = end_time (assuming they showed up on time)
        # But flag as 'late' if they actually checked in >10 min late (but we don't have actual times?)
        # And 'noshow' if they never checked in.
        
        # I think the most sensible interpretation given the initial data pattern is:
        # - check_in_time should be the shift start_time
        # - check_out_time should be the shift end_time  
        # - attendance_flag should be 'on_time' for everyone who checked in at start time
        # - volunteer_hours = (end - start) in hours
        
        # With this interpretation, since check_in = start, no one should be 'late'
        # Everyone should be 'on_time' or 'noshow'
        
        # But initial data shows late flags, so maybe the task is to update/create records
        # based on actual behavior, not ideal behavior?
        
        # Let me go with: if check_in_time = start_time, flag should be 'on_time'
        # This is the most logical given "record check_ins at their scheduled start_time"
        
        if check_in_dt == start_time:
            if attendance_flag not in ['on_time', None]:
                # Allow None as some systems might not set this
                # But task requires setting flags, so should be 'on_time'
                if attendance_flag != 'on_time':
                    return {"result": "others"}
    
    return {"result": "complete"}

def verify_task_completion(initial_db_path: str, final_db_path: str, final_answer: str | None = None) -> dict:
    import sqlite3
    import re

    def safe_query(db_path: str, query: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list:
        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(query, params)
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return results
        except Exception:
            return []

    LOT_ID = 5501
    EXPECTED_BID_AMOUNT = 260.00
    EXPECTED_AUTO_BID_MAX = 400.00
    
    # Check 1: Verify lot 5501 exists and get its auction_event_id
    lot_query = "SELECT auction_event_id, status FROM lots WHERE id = ?"

        return {"result": "others"}
    
    auction_event_id = lot_info[0][0]
    lot_status = lot_info[0][1]
    
    # Check 2: Verify auction_event is open
    event_query = "SELECT status FROM auction_events WHERE id = ?"
    event_info = safe_query(initial_db_path, event_query, (auction_event_id,))
    if not event_info or event_info[0][0] != 'open':
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 3: Verify initial highest bid is below 260.00
    initial_bid_stats = safe_query(initial_db_path, 
        "SELECT highest_bid_amount, number_of_bids FROM lot_bid_stats WHERE lot_id = ?",

    if not initial_bid_stats:

        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 4: Verify watchlist entry exists in final_db
    watchlist_query = "SELECT id FROM watchlists WHERE lot_id = ?"
    watchlist_entries = safe_query(final_db_path, watchlist_query, (LOT_ID,))
    if not watchlist_entries:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 5: Get initial bids for lot 5501
    initial_bids = safe_query(initial_db_path, 
        "SELECT id, bid_amount, auto_bid_max FROM lot_bids WHERE lot_id = ?", 
        (LOT_ID,))
    initial_bid_ids = {bid[0] for bid in initial_bids}
    
    # Check 6: Find new bid in final_db
    final_bids = safe_query(final_db_path, 
        "SELECT id, bid_amount, auto_bid_max FROM lot_bids WHERE lot_id = ?", 
        (LOT_ID,))
    
    new_bids = [bid for bid in final_bids if bid[0] not in initial_bid_ids]
    
    if not new_bids:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check if any new bid matches the expected values
    bid_found = False
    for bid in new_bids:
        bid_amount = bid[1]
        auto_bid_max = bid[2]
        
        # Allow small floating point tolerance
        if (abs(bid_amount - EXPECTED_BID_AMOUNT) < 0.01 and 
            auto_bid_max is not None and 
            abs(auto_bid_max - EXPECTED_AUTO_BID_MAX) < 0.01):
            bid_found = True
            break
    
    if not bid_found:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    # Check 7: Verify lot_bid_stats updated correctly
    final_bid_stats = safe_query(final_db_path, 
        "SELECT highest_bid_amount, number_of_bids FROM lot_bid_stats WHERE lot_id = ?", 
        (LOT_ID,))
    
    if not final_bid_stats:
        return {"result": "others"}
    
    final_highest_bid = final_bid_stats[0][0]
    final_bid_count = final_bid_stats[0][1]
    
    # Verify highest bid is now 260.00 and count increased
    if (final_highest_bid is not None and 
        abs(final_highest_bid - EXPECTED_BID_AMOUNT) < 0.01 and 
        final_bid_count > initial_bid_count):
        return {"result": "complete"}
    
    return {"result": "others"}

                    return {"result": "complete"}
                # If we can't verify 55922 status but everything else is correct, still accept
                elif offer_55922_final:
                    return {"result": "complete"}

    return {"result": "others"}
